chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Hadeed, from Jameel ibn Darraj, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him about a Mutamatti' (one who performs Umrah then Hajj) who shaved his head in Makkah. He said: If he was ignorant, there is nothing upon him; and if he deliberately did that in the beginning of the months of Hajj, within thirty days from it, there is nothing upon him; and if he deliberately did it after the thirty days during which the hair is allowed to grow for the Hajj, then upon him is a dam (blood/sacrifice) that he must spill.
And in another report, he said: So when it is the Day of Sacrifice (Yawm al-Nahr), he passes the razor over his head.

key_terms.أَشْهُرِ الْحَجِّ: The months of Hajj (Dhu al-Qi'dah, Dhu al-Hijjah, Shawwal, and part of Dhul-Hijjah).
key_terms.دَماً: Blood (referring to a sacrificial animal, i.e., dam).
key_terms.مُتَمَتِّعٍ: A pilgrim who performs Umrah and then Hajj in the same season, keeping their hair long between the two.
key_terms.يَوْمُ النَّحْرِ: The Day of Sacrifice (10th of Dhul-Hijjah, Eid al-Adha).

ai.seo_question: What is the penalty if a Mutamatti' pilgrim shaves his head before the proper time for Hajj?
ai.summary: This ruling from al-Kafi addresses the specific penalty for prematurely shaving during the Tamattu' Hajj, distinguishing between ignorance and deliberate intent, as well as the timing relative to the hair-growth period. The requirement of a 'dam' (sacrificial animal) for late, deliberate shaving underscores the importance of adhering to the sequential rites of Hajj, a concept rooted in the Quranic injunctions of Surah Al-Baqarah. The secondary report regarding the Day of Sacrifice highlights the ritual precision expected in the completion of the pilgrimage rites.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin hadeed, from Jameel Bin Darraj, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws, said, ‘I asked himasws about the performer of Tumatto shaving off his head in Makkah. Heasws said: ‘If he did not know, so there is nothing upon him; and if he deliberated that during the beginning of the month of Hajj by thirty days from it, so there is nothing upon him; and if he had deliberated after the thirty days which during which hairs are to be let grown for the Hall, so upon him is blood (of a sacrificial animal) he would have to spill’.
And in another report, ‘(He<sup>asws</sup> said): ‘So when it would be the day of the sacrifice, he would wipe the blade upon his head’.
en.sarwar: 7. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn Hadid from Jamil ibn Darraj who has said the following: “I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about a man who is for al-Hajj al-Tamattu‘ (advantageous) and has shaved his head in Makkah. He (the Imam) said, ‘If he is ignorant, he is not obligated for anything in this matter. If it is intentional and in the beginning of the months of al-Hajj by thirty days, there is not anything on him; but if it is done intentionally after thirty days during which hairs are left untouched for al-Hajj, then he owes one animal offering to slaughter.’”
NOTE: In another Hadith it is said that on the day of ‘Id he is required to pass a shaving blade on his head as if shaving.
